pl515280820.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl515280820.description: Village in southern Turkmenistan located near the Altyn Depe site, inhabited in the late Neolithic and Aeneolithic periods. The finds at the site have been dated from 6200-4350 BCE, with a hiatus in settlement from 5600-4800 BCE.

pl374540942.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl374540942.description: Chalcolithic settlement near Chaacha, Turkmenistan. This site was initially settled in the fifth millennium BCE, flourished in the mid-fourth, and was subsequently abandoned.

pl377547413.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl377547413.description: A Bronze Age urban settlement, associated with the Jiroft culture, located in Sistan and Baluchistan provinces in the southeastern part of Iran. The site was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2014.

pl85264970.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl85264970.description: An ancient, proto-urban site located in north-western Tajikistan.

pl29678.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl29678.description: A large site in modern Afghanistan's Nimruz province. Archaeological evidence is abundant for habitation during the third - first millennia BCE, as well as 8th - 13th centuries CE, when Nād ʿAlī was clearly a major fortified urban center.

pl842000735.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl842000735.description: Large settlement of the late Neolothic period through the Bronze Age located in modern Turkmenistan. Part of the Bactria–Margiana Archaeological Complex, Altyn-Depe was a major urban center of Bronze Age Central Asia.

pl705861784.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl705861784.description: Small settlement located approximately 10km southeast of Shahr-i Sokhta in the Sistan Plain, eastern Iran, inhabited from the first half of the 3rd millennium BCE until approximately 2350 BCE.

pl491632348.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl491632348.description: A cemetery site in southern Tajikistan containing burials from the Vaksh culture (mid-late 3rd millennium BCE).

pl391537222.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl391537222.description: A city in the Murghab River delta inhabited in the third-second millennia BCE. Gonur Tepe is located ca. 60 km north of Mary, Turkmenistan.

pl498033127.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl498033127.description: Mundigak is an archaeological site in Afghanistan's Kandahar province where evidence for a 'palace' belonging to the Harappan transitional phase has been discovered.

q214495.dateNote: The date 2800 BC can not be confirmed. Bamyan is best known as a Buddhist centre from the first centuries AD.

pl971796.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl971796.description: Khush Tepe, also known as Tepe Fullol, is a burial site associated with the Oxus Civilization. Discovered in 1966, the site contained gold and silver vessels dated to the Bronze Age (ca. 2600-1700 BCE).

pl646531235.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl646531235.description: Proto-urban settlement and necropolis site located in the Surxondaryo region, Uzbekistan.

pl717754049.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl717754049.description: An ancient trading colony on the Oxus river in the vicinity of the lapis lazuli mines of northern Afghanistan dating to ca. 2000 BC.

pl469183602.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl469183602.description: Bactrian site in southwestern Tajikistan containing a settlement and burial ground dated to the Bronze and early Iron Ages.

pl961886.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl961886.description: An ancient city of what is now northern Afghanistan. Bactra/Zariaspa (modern Balkh) was a center of Zoroastrianism.

pl875060625.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl875060625.description: Necropolis in Southern Uzbekistan with late Bronze Age remains.

pl29718.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl59694.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl60476.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl60476.description: The site of Cartana/Karnasa/Tetrogonis remains unlocated, although scholars have advanced various theories as to its location.

pl961874.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl630721027.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl630721027.description: Tradition holds that the Iron Age and Achaemenid citadel of Old Kandahar was re-established during the time of Alexander the Great. It functioned as a local seat of power for at least two millennia.

pl59747.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl59747.description: An ancient settlement, located at modern Lashkargāh (formerly Bost/Boost) in Helmand province, Afghanistan.

pl961971.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl961971.description: Yaz tepe was an ancient settlement located in southeastern Turkmenistan.

pl971895.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl29540.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl29540.description: A mud brick urban site in Sīstān, Iran, with a main period of occupation around the fifth century BCE. It was probably the Achaemenid provincial capital of Zarin or Zranka in Drangiana until it was buried by sand or dried out by movements of the Helmand endorheic basin.

pl961872.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl961875.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl961875.description: Altin Dilyar tepe is a place located in Afghanistan's Balkh Province. It lies to the north of Balkh, about 22 km south of the Oxus River (Amu Darya) and 16 kilometers north of Daulatabad, according to Ball (1982: 38). The ceramic evidence on the site belongs to the Achaemenid period, ca. sixth to fourth centuries BCE. Ball also notes that there is evidence for "a circular walled town covering approximately 15 hectares, dominated by a central citadel, 28 meters high." The site remains unexcavated.

pl971886.description: Termez, located in modern Uzbekistan, was part of the Graeco-Bactrian kingdom and later the Kushan empire. It eventually became an important center of Buddhism.

pl59669.description: Now Kandahar in Afghanistan, Alexandria/Alexandropolis/Cufis is an ancient site founded by Alexander the Great ca. 330 BC. The indigenous people of the Hellenistic period were likely the Pakthas.

pl935832829.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl935832829.description: Erk Kala, founded in the sixth century B.C., was at the center of Merv.

pl310634609.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl310634609.description: Qa`la Bost is an ancient fortress within the ancient city of Bust, located on the Helmand River in southern Afghanistan and overseeing a major crossroads linking Kandahar and India to eastern Iran. Standing remains at the site predominantly date to the Islamic Middle Ages, but archaeological finds suggest an occupational history dating back to at least the first millennium BCE.

pl29457.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl29525.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl697343073.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl697343073.description: This "Mesopotamian-style temple" site located near modern Dishu in Afghanistan's Helmand province was excavated in the 1970s. Carbon-14 dates and "Greek-style architectural fragments and fine red pottery" led the excavators to date the use of the site from the late Hellenistic and Parthian period to "the beginning of the Sasanian period in the 3rd century" CE. Finds included a fragmentary bilingual (Greek/Aramaic) inscription possibly mentioning a Parthian king Phraates and the Iranian deity Ahuramazda.

pl809369795.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl809369795.description: An archaeological site located in the Surxondaryo Region of Uzbekistan, in proximity to the city of Termez. Its ancient identification is uncertain.

pl332324145.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl332324145.description: The fortifications of the ancient city of Gyaur Kala in the Merv Oasis.

pl59668.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl59668.description: "Alexandria in the Caucasus", an Achaemenid town re-established by Alexander the Great at modern Charikar, near Bagram in Afghanistan.

pl59915.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl59915.description: Marakanda (now Samarkand in Uzbekistan) was a major ancient settlement founded ca. 700 BC by the Sogdians. Alexander the Great conquered Marakanda during his eastern campaigns.

pl60105.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl562472667.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl562472667.description: The Temple of the Oxus is a Seleucid-era temple situated within the citadel of Takhti-Sangin, a Graeco-Bactrian town between the Vakhsh and Panj rivers.

pl122728089.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl122728089.description: Monumental statues of Gautam Buddha were carved into the cliff-face at Bamyan, located in the Bamyan valley in the Hazarajat region of central Afghanistan, The statues were, respectively, 35 and 53 m tall. They were intentionally destroyed by the Taliban in 2001.

pl961878.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl961878.description: At Aq Chapur 1 there is evidence of a monumental building surrounded by two fortified enclosures. At Aq Chapur 2 was a large monument similar to that of Aq Chapar 1. This site is surrounded by a defensive wall with reinforcing towers.

pl961880.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl961893.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl961896.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl961901.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl961901.description: Dilbarjin is an ancient city of northern Afghanistan. The site may have been founded under the Achaemenid Empire. Under the Kushan Empire, the site was a fortified local center of some importance.

pl961905.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl961905.description: Emshi tepe is located in Jauzjan Province to the northeast of Shibarghan. Material on the site dates to the Hellenistic, Kushan, and Sassanian/Kushano-Sassanian periods.

pl961907.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl961918.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl961918.description: A site located in Balkh Province, east of Dilbarjin. The material observed at the site dates to the Hellenistic, Kushan, and Early Sasanian periods.

pl961923.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl961924.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl961959.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl971693.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl971693.description: Ai Khanoum is an archaeological site near the modern town of Dast-i-Qal'a in Afghanistan's Takhar Province. It is probably to be identified with the attested name "Alexandria Oxiana" (Alexandria on Oxus), which was founded in the fourth century BCE in the wake of the campaigns of Alexander the Great. It was a chief city of the Graeco-Bactrian kingdom, but was abandoned around 145 BCE.

pl971696.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl971696.description: An ancient city that, according to Arrian, was destroyed by Alexander the Great. It is perhaps to be associated with modern Khulm (formerly Tashkurgan) in Afghanistan.

pl971701.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl971746.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl971746.description: Drapsaka (modern Kunduz) was an ancient settlement in central Asia.

pl971880.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl971882.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl971882.description: Takht-i Sangin is an ancient settlement located near the confluence of the Vakhsh and Panj rivers. It may be the source of the so-called "Oxus Treasure".

pl971894.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl971894.description: A large, fortified Kushan urban center (first to third centuries).

pl971899.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl971899.description: An archaeological site with evidence of three settlement mounds. Phases of identifiable human activity include the Hellenistic period at Mound B (3rd-1st century B.C.) and Hepthalo-Turk (5th-9th century A.D.) at Mounds A and C. Traces of Islamic activity also were detected.

pl752130724.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl752130724.description: A large oasis settlement north of modern Shahrisabz in Uzbekistan that included the fortress of Uzunqïr. It is thought to be the location of ancient Kish/Kesh and possibly the Nautaka mentioned in Hellenistic Greco-Roman sources.

pl473795769.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl473795769.description: A settlement site in modern Uzbekistan's Pamir-Alay mountain range dating probably between the second century BCE and the first century CE.

pl988662689.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl988662689.description: Dasht-e Nawar is a settlement site beginning in prehistoric times on the shores of the lake of the same name. Based on epigraphic evidence, the Archaeological Gazetteer of Afghanistan (1982) classifies it as Kushan, second-third century AD.

pl29800.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl961969.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl961969.description: Tillya tepe ("Golden Hill" or "Golden Mound") is an archaeological site in northern Afghanistan near Sheberghan. A hoard of approx. 20,000 gold ornaments and coins were discovered in six tombs dating to the first century BC.

pl569531630.description: Minar-i Chakri, located in the Kabul province of Afghanistan, was the site of a Kushan-era pillar dating to the second or third century AD that was destroyed in the later twentieth century by the Soviet army.

cur-fossil-teshik-tash.dateNote: In 1938 Alexey Okladnikov found the skeleton of a Neanderthal child in this cave in Uzbekistan, ringed by goat horns. It is about 70,000 years old (0.07 million years), the furthest east a Neanderthal was known for decades.
